title: Tenali Raman Tale 87 (हिन्दी)

full_text:
A flamboyant palmist and astrologer named Jyotishi Shankara set up an ornate canopy in the main bazaar of Vijayanagara, wearing an enormous turban of gold-threaded silk adorned with peacock feathers.
He proclaimed to the crowds:
'I read the lines of destiny with absolute infallibility! I foresee all events that will occur to any man ten years into the future!'
Citizens paid silver coins to hear flattering prophecies of wealth and marriage.

Tenali Raman walked past the booth, observing the charlatan fleece poor laborers.
Tenali decided to demonstrate the fraud before the entire bazaar.

Tenali stood in the crowd, watching the astrologer hold a customer’s palm.
Tenali quietly untied his light bamboo walking staff.
With a swift, deft, upward flick of his staff, Tenali hooked the brim of the astrologer's magnificent golden turban, flicked it off the man’s head, and sent it flying straight into an open basket of fresh, sticky black dates at the neighboring fruit stall!

The turban landed upside down with a wet squelch, completely smothered in black date syrup and squashed fruit!

The astrologer leaped up, bareheaded and bald, shrieking in furious outrage:
'Insolent villain! Who knocked off my golden turban? Who ruined my expensive silk hat?'

Tenali Raman stepped forward, smiling with delightful innocence:
'Why, great Astrologer! You claimed to foresee the fate of every stranger ten years into the future!
How is it that with all your celestial vision, you could not foresee that your own turban would fly into a basket of sticky dates five seconds ago?
If your stars cannot warn you about your own hat, how dare you charge silver to predict the life of another man?'

The entire marketplace erupted in roaring laughter!
The customers demanded their silver back, laughing at the bald astrologer struggling to scrape date syrup from his ruined turban.
The charlatan packed his charts and fled Vijayanagara, while Tenali showed that practical proof easily dismantles false claims of omniscience.
moral: Those who claim to foresee the distant future of strangers cannot even foresee the loss of their own hats. [HI]
